A.note: tight can-on-a-nail arc and good jokes, but Cairn appears only in ch3 so his ask feels sudden

B.note: Cairn watches from ch1 ('stones round up'), rain shelter beat is lovely; the strongest bond with the gardener

C.note: warm grassling-on-the-moss opening, but Cairn never speaks before the ask and the gardener's two-line monologues feel formulaic

valley.graft: A ch3, gardener: "the beds did fine without me. a bit rude of them, really."

A.note: dry, funny drover ('the dog's a terrible influence', 'show-offs'); Tally appears only in ch3

B.note: Tally counts from ch1 and brings the flock in herself, so her ask is clearly earned; the socks gag is sweet

C.note: great drover lines and a strong moonrise ending, but Tally is thin and the ask is generic

brackens.graft: C ch1, drover: "can't stop, mind. a drover who stops is just a man standing in a field."

A.note: collar-on-a-peg arc is clean and 'tuesday's nice' is perfect; Puddle is a light presence

B.note: Clover has a name, Puddle grows across all three chapters, and 'forty years on that rope and the sea was just over the hill' lands the theme

C.note: 'a plant having a nap, not a carrot' charms, but Puddle gets one line before the ask

lull.graft: A ch3, bargee: "we'll go when she wakes. or tuesday. tuesday's nice."

A.note: kettle moved to the cool side is a fine concrete step; 'hot was just showing off' is a highlight

B.note: Tam notices she never drinks a cup, makes her one, then keeps the bothy: the most personal ask in the set

C.note: the blanket over the grassling is warm, but 'always... up' and 'so am i, a bit' feel half-landed and Tam is thin

frostline.graft: A ch2, warden: "it stays warm there. warm is plenty. hot was just showing off."

A.note: watch in her hand, then lid shut, then on a nail: crisp, with Pendle's deadpan 'mostly quiet. some pigeons.'

B.note: Pendle kept the slow minute 'very well polished' and gives it back; 'i decided that a minute ago' is the best ask in the set

C.note: 'i didn't time it. i did time it.' is very funny, but the ch1 grassling-found pattern repeats

cogsworth.graft: A ch3, Pendle: "mostly quiet. some pigeons."

A.note: tally-book arc with a pleasing blank page; Tuff only arrives in ch3, though 'it hums in g' is lovely

B.note: Tuff's ellipsis voice is distinctive and inches nearer each chapter; 'they're really just the one, aren't they' is the emotional peak

C.note: 'one grassling. sleeping. noted.' is charming, but Tuff appears only at the end

isles.graft: A ch3, Tuff: "i've been listening for a few thousand years. it hums in g."

A.note: the outlet stone is a good image, but 'one scoop a day' reads like a routine chore and the trader's voice is generic salesman

B.note: the trader ladles faster 'so the pool wouldn't notice' and Mirra drives the discovery; clear and warm, a little earnest

C.note: the 'don't tell anyone' callback is charming; Mirra gets one line before her ask

sunstone.graft: C ch3, trader: "creek's running through the gulch. i'm not charging for it. don't tell anyone."

A.note: banked white to red, then asleep; Ashe's 'it's the best colour i go' is the warmest beat in the region

B.note: two bells is a strong opening and Ashe carrying the bell down is good, but the lines are a touch stiff ('by the bell, smith')

C.note: 'banked one keeps' is a strong moral in plain words; the smith's opening glare is fun, but Ashe is thin

fire.graft: B ch2, Ashe: "she heard it. she put the hammer down. then picked it up. that is progress."

A.note: a likeable Dave ('weirdly okay?') and the blanket ordered two years ago is a great payoff

B.note: Nix's 'status:' log voice is perfect, the parcel-to-blanket arc is cohesive, and 'oh. it's me. i'm quiet.' is the line of the set

C.note: 'in this economy' is a great Dave line, but ch3's spot (the falls) clashes with his bench, and Nix is thin

neon.graft: A ch2, Dave: "it's like a feed, but it's all the same post. weirdly okay?"

A.note: 'tidiest bunk on the station. nobody's ever used it' is very good; Bunk's visor joke is muddled

B.note: 'tucked in forty-one sleepers. zero keepers.' plus magnetic mugs: Bunk earns the ask

C.note: 'who'd fluff the fluffer?' and 'i'd recommend it to me' are the funniest lines in the region; Bunk is thin

halcyon.graft: C ch3, keeper: "i tested a bunk myself. eight hours. very good. i'd recommend it to me."

A.note: 'it wasn't lost. it was asleep. you find it with your eyes shut' is a beautiful finale and Mote is 'keeping it warm'; Mote is late

B.note: Mote as the gap from ch1 with her 'mm' voice, and 'shall we finish it together?' gives the fourteenth folk the right weight

C.note: 'everyone we met is resting somewhere' is a moving journey's end, but two-line stargazer monologues again

lumen.graft: A ch1, stargazer: "stars don't hide. they're terrible at it." (or A ch3's "you find it with your eyes shut")
